free_tier.stated: paid $1.35/TB/month stored + $1.00/TB egress (cut from $1.50/$2.00 on 1 Sep 2026, an 18% total reduction). Paid in USDC on Ethereum, not STORJ.

egress.terms: you are paid $1.00/TB for egress; the customer is charged $7/TB

interface_detail: Docker container, single identity per node, dashboard
tooling: storagenode Docker image, storj node dashboard, uptime robot
chaining: USDC payout can be spent on anything, but cannot be converted into Storj storage credit - there is no credit mechanism
limits_note: Worse ratio than Sia and stated in the same currency, which makes it unambiguous: SNO gets $1.35/TB while Storj charges the customer $7.00/TB for the same terabyte - a 5.2x gap. To fund 20 TiB at $7/TB ($140/mo) plus 30 TiB/mo egress at $7/TB ($210/mo) = $350/mo, you must store $350/1.35 = 259 TB of other people's data. Storj's own forum arithmetic also carries a 2.7x erasure expansion factor, so 1 TB of customer data consumes 2.7 TB of SNO disk - meaning the true disk ratio is ~700 TB contributed to consume 20 TB. This is the clearest negative in the slot.
reliability_note: Node disqualification and held amounts apply for the first months; forum reports of 8.5 TiB stored paying $5.50 indicate realised rates well below list.
